fact: Tom Allen was born in Birmingham, England.
Tom Allen fought Joe Goss in March 1867, and his right shoulder was dislocated in the 25th round, but he fought on; he was then 27 years old and 5 feet 10 inches tall.
After the 1867 fight a mob attacked Tom Allen, and he was shot in the hand and hit in the eye with a club.
Coburn knocked Tom Allen off the stage at the Bowery Theater in 1868, slightly injuring him.
Tom Allen's brother Harry Allen was matched to fight Joe Goss for £400 and the championship of England on September 4, 1868, and Harry died soon after the planned fight was stopped.
The paper gave Tom Allen's age as 28 at the time of a fight on January 12, 1869.
Tom Allen was knocked senseless on February 23, 1869, and lay unconscious until Looney doctored him; he was then 28 years old, 5 feet 9 inches tall and weighed 168 pounds.
After a June 1869 fight Tom Allen, reported as 28 years old, had only a slight abrasion of the lower lip.
In June 1869 Tom Allen's English sweetheart was reported to be joining him, and to be going with him toward St. Louis to marry him.

In 1869 Tom Allen said he had declared his intention to become a United States citizen two years earlier, and in August 1869 he claimed to be an American citizen and said he would fight under American colors.
Tom Allen was said to be sick at the time of the July 1869 meeting for drawing up the articles of his fight with Mike McCoole.
Tom Allen fought Charley Gallagher at Chouteau Island on August 17, 1869, and a shot struck the back of his right hand.
Tom Allen was very sick for about a week before December 16, 1869, and was confined to his house.
Tom Allen fought Jem Mace at New Orleans on May 10, 1870, and was injured in the fight.
Tom Allen has a sister who teaches school in Corydon, Indiana.
The paper gave Tom Allen's age as about 37 in June 1870.
On June 10, 1873, Tom Allen weighed about 200 pounds and was in good health.
Tom Allen fought Mike McCoole on September 23, 1873, and a knuckle on his right hand was slightly cut.
Tom Allen and Ben Hogan fought on October 28, 1873, and both were in excellent condition on the day of the fight; Allen weighed 172 pounds stripped on October 24.
Tom Allen was struck with a rock before the Edwards-Collyer fight in August 1874 but received no damage from it.
In March 1875 Tom Allen was reported to be 36 years old.
In March 1875 Tom Allen weighed about 210 pounds, was in fine health but still quite fleshy, and would have to train down to 172 pounds to fight.
In July 1875 Tom Allen had a family to care for.
In September 1876 Tom Allen was four years younger than his opponent, Joe Goss.
After his September 1876 fight with Joe Goss, Tom Allen had only a slight mark on his upper lip and a swollen right hand, and a paper said he looked the very picture of physical health.
In September 1876 a paper said Tom Allen's accent showed his nationality, without naming it.
Tom Allen's daughter Mary, called Polly, returned to the United States with him and later married Edward Taylor of St. Louis.
In 1882 Tom Allen had a severe attack of sea-sickness crossing the ocean, from which he had just recovered.
In January 1882 a mob of roughs at Cork, Ireland, attacked Tom Allen and cut and bruised him so badly that his life was despaired of.
In November 1882 Tom Allen was 43 years old, according to the Boston Star.
On 5 December 1882 Tom Allen said he had been sick and had not left the house since his exhibition.
On 29 December 1882 Tom Allen said he was as well as ever, though he had a sore throat from a slight cold.
In September 1885 Tom Allen was an incorrigible bachelor, and hints of marriage had come to nothing.
After the June 1888 street fight Tom Allen had a cut and discoloured ear, an abrasion on the left jaw, a black eye and a bruise on the side of his face.
Tom Allen's birthday was celebrated on 23 April 1892.

Tom Allen was thrown from his buggy on Saturday 10 September 1892 when his horse became uncontrollable on his usual afternoon drive, and was confined to bed from 13 September with a painful illness from the shaking up.
In March 1895 Tom Allen was described as 54 years old.
In May 1896 Tom Allen was reported as not badly hurt; the sentence is cut off in the scan.
On 1 July 1898 Tom Allen was badly punished in an attack and was saved from serious injury when his barkeeper came to his rescue just in time.
In March 1900 Tom Allen's daughter lived in the building where he ran his concert hall and had devoted her life to caring for him.
Tom Allen had been ill since Christmas 1902 and was convalescing in March and April 1903.
Tom Allen was seriously ill in early 1903, confined to his bed for weeks with persistent colds at his home on Market Street, and his manager Don Murphy said he would soon be out again.
Tom Allen planned to marry his nurse and housekeeper, Mrs. Tillie Hartgrove of St. Louis, once he recovered, on his birthday, 23 April 1903.
Tom Allen was taken to the Baptist Hospital at Garrison and Franklin avenues, St. Louis, on 28 March 1903, after the physician diagnosed pneumonia and advised removal; he was seriously ill there.

Allen's daughter, Mrs. Mary Taylor, went to the Baptist Hospital on 30 March 1903 with Robert Lyons and was refused admittance, having been told her father was too ill to talk to anyone after the report of his engagement.
Mrs. Taylor said her mother and sister were living in Birmingham, England.
Tom Allen died at the Baptist Hospital, Garrison and Franklin avenues, St. Louis, early on Sunday 5 April 1903, at the age of 6-, and his body lay at an undertaking establishment.

Tom Allen was buried in St. Louis on Wednesday 8 April 1903, after a funeral from an undertaking establishment, with pallbearers including former prize fighters, his daughter standing by the coffin with her four children, and the funeral procession going to the cemetery.
Some retrospective articles placed Tom Allen's death in St. Louis in 1904 or 1905.
